messages:
maya: heads up — I experimented with a 'noise_mode' dropdown in the SLO editor to reduce alert storms from low-traffic tenants. options: conservative | aggressive | sampled | mute. put a quick preview in the notify panel but seeing odd counts on the preview for tenants with <10 req/min.

jonah: can you paste the config you used? curious which percentile + window we defaulted to.

maya: sure — pasted below. preview is from notify-preview for a 5% error budget breach. note that sampled mode should fraction alerts, but preview shows full fanout.

maya: ```json
{
  "slo": {
    "metric": "latency_ms",
    "objective": "p95 < 300",
    "window": "5m",
    "noise_mode": "sampled",
    "sample_rate": 0.2,
    "group_by": ["tenant_id"]
  },
  "notify": {
    "channels": ["pagerduty", "email"],
    "preview": true
  }
}
```

li: aha — two things to check: (1) notify-preview runs in deterministic mode and ignores sample_rate so UX shows worst-case fanout, (2) our notify API was treating sample_rate as per-route but not per-tenant, so small tenants got rounded up. both easy fixes but need decision on preview semantics.

ashley: from product POV: prefer preview shows both worst-case and expected fanout. customers asked for conservative worst-case to plan paging, but ops want expected to avoid surprises. maybe show both numbers?

jonah: agree. technically we can compute two values: worst_case_count and expected_count. expected_count uses sample_rate and traffic estimate. but that requires us to fetch recent traffic telemetry for the tenant which we currently hide behind the telemetry read API (permissions).

product-ux: if we add dual numbers make UX simple: a small inline badge "expected: 1.2 alerts, worst-case: 6 alerts" and tooltip explaining sampled mode. also add a link "why preview differs from live" to docs.

maya: one more wrinkle — during canary rollouts Dedicated triggers can create simultaneous transient breaches across zones. folks suggested an auto-snooze during rollouts or an opt-in 'suppress-during-rollout' flag. any strong opinions?

li: auto-snooze sounds dangerous. we already have a rollout hook in the routing layer that tags requests. better is: allow notify rules to include an allowlist on request_tag=rollout so rules can exclude these events. keep it explicit.

jonah: +1 for explicit. also we should add a warning when someone sets objective with p99 on 1m windows for low traffic tenants — the SLO editor should surface "unstable stat" and suggest longer windows or count-based thresholds.

ashley: can we add a small inline recommendation engine? e.g., "suggested: change to p95 or increase window to 1h" with a quick apply button. That would reduce friction for ops.

maya: yep. that's part of the Optimize work — we can reuse the cost/perf heuristics. will prototype.

sre-bot: incident: high-alert-volume detected in tenant: alpha-test at 2026-03-19T12:03:05Z — reason: rollout spike. auto-ticket created: #INC-6123.

jonah: we should ensure bot checks the notify rule's 'suppress_during_rollout' flag before creating tickets. otherwise the bot will undo any suppression attempt.

li: action items: 1) change notify-preview to show expected + worst-case (maya), 2) telemetry read permission gate for preview (infra/eng-plat), 3) don't ignore sample_rate in preview (maya), 4) expose explicit rollout-exclusion tag in notify API (eng-runtime), 5) UX microcopy for unstable stats + quick suggestions (product-ux).

maya: i'll open a draft PR for preview logic and add a screenshot of dual numbers. assigning followups in a comment on the PR. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

product-ux: thanks maya — will mock the badge and tooltip by EOD.

jonah: tagging @ashley to review the messaging for enterprise docs — it'll need legal signoff for "mute" semantics.

ashley: noted. I'll loop in compliance.

maya: ok last note — watch out for per-tenant grouping edge-case: if group_by has both tenant_id and route, aggregation can explode previews. i suggest we cap preview expansion to top-10 groups and show a "+N groups" link.

product-ux: nice. that keeps preview compact.

maya: great. closing thread for now, will post PR link when ready.
